text: One day Tom took a shortcut through the swamp. <break time="0.8s" /> A gloomy place. <break time="0.8s" /> Where tall pines and hemlocks. <break time="0.8s" /> Made it dark even at noon. <break time="0.8s" /> Moving as carefully as a cat. <break time="0.8s" /> He picked his way along fallen tree trunks. <break time="0.8s" /> For green moss hid. <break time="0.8s" /> Deep pools of black mud. <break time="0.8s" /> At last he reached a firm piece of ground. <break time="0.8s" /> Where Native Americans had once built a fort. <break time="0.8s" /> During their wars with the first settlers. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting down on a fallen tree to rest. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom poked at the soil with his stick. <break time="0.8s" /> And turned up an old skull. <break time="0.8s" /> From those wars. <break time="0.8s" /> Lifting his eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom saw a huge stranger. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting on a stump right in front of him. <break time="0.8s" /> Though he had not heard anyone approach. <break time="0.8s" /> The mans face was dark and dirty with soot. <break time="0.8s" /> As if he worked among fires. <break time="0.8s" /> And a heavy axe rested on his shoulder. <break time="0.8s" /> What are you doing on my grounds. <break time="0.8s" /> Growled the stranger. <break time="0.8s" /> But Tom answered. <break time="0.8s" /> That the land belonged to Deacon Peabody. <break time="0.8s" /> The stranger pointed to a tall tree. <break time="0.8s" /> Which looked healthy on the outside. <break time="0.8s" /> But was rotten at the core. <break time="0.8s" /> With Peabodys name carved on its bark. <break time="0.8s" /> Nearby lay another great tree. <break time="0.8s" /> Already cut down. <break time="0.8s" /> Which bore the name of Crowninshield. <break time="0.8s" /> A rich man. <break time="0.8s" /> Said to have made his fortune as a pirate.
